holidays.name: National Kiss a Wookiee Day
holidays.description: Star Wars fans honor Chewbacca by giving a (hopefully willing) hug or kiss to their favorite walking carpet. Fans celebrate with marathons, Wookiee roars, and fuzzy costumes.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial fan-created observance rooted in Star Wars fandom. It is a playful nod to Princess Leia's famous parting line to Chewbacca.
holidays.funFact: Chewbacca's famous roar was built from recordings of real animals, including a bear named Tarra, mixed with other animal sounds by sound designer Ben Burtt.

holidays.name: National Megalodon Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the biggest shark that ever lived, a prehistoric predator with teeth as big as a human hand. Fans of sharks, fossils and monster movies get to geek out.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial observance of unclear origin. It celebrates Otodus megalodon, the giant shark that swam the oceans millions of years ago.
holidays.funFact: Megalodon is estimated to have reached roughly 50 to 60 feet long, and its fossilized teeth can top 7 inches. Scientists still debate its exact size because only teeth and a few vertebrae have been found.

holidays.name: National Lobster Day
holidays.description: A day to crack open a buttery lobster tail, roll a lobster roll, or just admire the red-shelled crustacean. It is a favorite among seafood lovers and New England summer fans.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance that celebrates lobster, particularly the Maine lobster tied to the New England coast.
holidays.funFact: Lobster was once considered poor people's food in colonial New England. It was fed to prisoners and used as fertilizer before it became a luxury.
